assessments.reasoning: MDC/28 §§3.2.2 and 3.2.3 on printed I-9 and I-10 explicitly allow unsubscripted and subscripted variable forms. The scan confirms the caret in the global production and its explanation, where OCR rendered the caret inconsistently. Both sections allow the bare occurrence to carry a different value from a subscripted occurrence.

challenge.method: Compare the ordinary local and global productions with indirection, naked global abbreviation, and the published YottaDB distinctions between local and database-backed variables. Check the scan glyph against the text layer.
challenge.results: The first two productions directly support the named forms and independent values. The caret is visually unambiguous. Indirection can produce a reference, and a naked form can obtain a name from the indicator. The named-form syntax does not establish process scope, persistence or storage implementation.

limitations: The finding is scoped to variable reference forms in the March 1975 MDC/28 narrative and its January 1976 NBS printing.
